Normalize the counts

Source: R/normalize_data.R
normalize_data.Rd

Sets the normalization of a ScreenR object, so that samples sequenced at different depths can be compared. The raw counts are not changed: the normalization is the effective library size of each sample, and the normalized count of a barcode is its raw count divided by the effective library size of its sample, times 1e6 (counts per million). Three methods are available:

  • "cpm" (default): the effective library size is the total number of reads of the sample;

  • "tmm": the total number of reads multiplied by the trimmed mean of M-values (TMM) normalization factor of edgeR (normLibSizes). This is more robust when strong hits deplete a large part of the library;

  • "control": the number of reads of the control barcodes (for example non-targeting shRNAs, or the sgRNAs of non-essential genes) of the sample. This assumes that the control barcodes are not affected by the treatment.

Usage

normalize_data(
  screenR_Object,
  method = c("cpm", "tmm", "control"),
  control_barcodes = NULL
)

Arguments

screenR_Object

The ScreenR object obtained using create_screenr_object.

method

The normalization method: "cpm" (default), "tmm" or "control".

control_barcodes

The identifiers of the control barcodes for the "control" method (required by that method, ignored by the others). Identifiers that are not in the object give a warning; if none is in the object, it is an error.

Value

The normalized ScreenR object.

Details

The normalization is used consistently by the whole analysis: the normalized counts (get_normalized_count_table), the data table (get_data_table) and everything computed from it (compute_metrics, plot_trend, plot_boxplot, compute_slope, ...), the sample plots (plot_mds, plot_pca, plot_replicate_correlation) and the edgeR and limma models (create_edger_obj, used by find_camera_hit, find_roast_hit, compute_barcode_statistics, find_time_hit, filter_by_variance and plot_barcode_hit), whose offsets are the logarithms of the effective library sizes. The models always use the raw counts. Logarithms and pseudocounts used by the plots (for example log2(normalized + 1) in plot_pca) are display transformations: they do not change the normalization.

It is stored in the object: the effective library sizes in the EffectiveLibSize column of the colData, the method and its provenance in the metadata (see get_normalization). Replacing the counts removes it; subsetting the object keeps the effective library sizes of the retained samples (call normalize_data() again to normalize on the retained barcodes only). Calling normalize_data() again replaces the normalization, and every view of the object follows immediately.

Every sample must have reads (and, for "control", reads of the control barcodes): a sample with an effective library size of zero cannot be normalized and is an error.

Choosing the method. In a dropout screen many barcodes are depleted, so with "cpm" all the other barcodes look enriched. "tmm" reduces this bias, but it assumes that most barcodes do not change and that the changes go in both directions: when many barcodes change in the same direction it corrects only part of the bias (in a simulation with 20% of the genes depleted 8 times it removed about half of it). "control" removes it when control barcodes known to be without effect are available (for example the sgRNAs of non-essential genes).

See also

get_normalization, create_edger_obj, get_normalized_count_table, remove_all_zero_row

Examples

object <- get0("object", envir = asNamespace("ScreenR"))
object <- normalize_data(object)
get_normalization(object)$method
#> [1] "cpm"
get_normalized_count_table(object)
#> ScreenR normalized count table: 5320 rows, 15 columns
